questions.q: What is globalisation, and which factors have enabled it?

answer.text: Globalisation is the process of rapid integration or interconnection between countries. It takes place through greater foreign trade and greater movement of capital, and increasingly through the spread of production itself by multinational corporations across many countries.

The single biggest factor has been rapid improvement in technology. Faster transport such as containers and jet aircraft has cut the cost and time of carrying goods over long distances, while information technology, the internet and telecommunication have made instant contact and remote control of production possible.

Governments have removed many barriers to trade and investment, a process called liberalisation, and the World Trade Organisation encourages countries to open up their trade, though its rules often favour developed nations.

answer: Together these forces have tied the economies of the world closely together.

questions.q: Has globalisation been fair to all? Examine its impact in India.
answer: Globalisation has brought both gains and losses, and its benefits have not been shared equally.

answer.text: For well-off consumers there is now greater choice, better quality and lower prices for goods such as cars, electronics and mobile phones. It has created new jobs in industries and in services like information technology, and some Indian companies such as Tata Motors and Infosys have themselves become multinationals.

At the same time, many small producers and workers have suffered. Small manufacturers of goods like toys and batteries have been hurt by cheap imports, and workers face job insecurity and poor conditions as firms cut costs.
So globalisation has not been fair to all. A fair globalisation needs the government to protect workers and small producers and to press for fair rules at the WTO.

answer: Only then can its benefits reach the poor as well as the rich.
